suggestions.name: Realistic Vision 5.1 (inpainting)
suggestions.what: An inpainting version of Realistic Vision that repaints a masked area of a photo so it blends in cleanly.
suggestions.howToUse: Choose it as your checkpoint when you use Edit. The author recommends the Euler A or DPM++ 2M Karras sampler and CFG 3.5 to 7, and says version 5.1 looks better with the sd-vae-ft-mse VAE (see Quality below). Their suggested negative prompt starts with: (deformed iris, deformed pupils, semi-realistic, cgi, 3d, render, sketch, cartoon, drawing, anime:1.4), text, cropped, worst quality, low quality, jpeg artifacts, ugly.
suggestions.license: CreativeML OpenRAIL-M

suggestions.name: DreamShaper 8 (inpainting)
suggestions.what: An inpainting version of DreamShaper 8, an all-round art and photo model, for fixing or replacing parts of an image.
suggestions.howToUse: Use it only for Edit (inpainting and outpainting), not for plain Generate; the author says it is not meant for txt2img. Its page gives no inpainting numbers, so start with the Strength (denoise) you normally use and adjust it yourself.

suggestions.name: Juggernaut XL (inpainting, Version X)
suggestions.what: An inpainting version of Juggernaut XL that gives smoother edits and fewer visible seams when extending or fixing a photo.
suggestions.howToUse: Use it for Edit. The author suggests the DPM++ 2M Karras sampler, 30 or more steps, CFG 2 to 7, and a denoising strength starting at 0.8 (try 0.6 if it gets too creative, or up to 0.9 to remove a stubborn detail).
suggestions.license: Civitai terms: generated images may be sold; merges and derivatives allowed; credit the author

suggestions.name: Animagine XL 3.1 (inpainting)
suggestions.what: An inpainting version of Animagine XL 3.1 for editing anime and illustration images.
suggestions.howToUse: Use it for Edit on anime-style pictures. The author uses CFG 2 to 7 and a denoising strength starting at 0.8 (0.6 if it strays from the surrounding colours, up to 0.9 to remove a detail). For prompts, see the Animagine XL 3.1 page.
suggestions.license: Civitai terms: generated images may be sold; merges and derivatives allowed

suggestions.name: Realistic Vision 5.1
suggestions.what: A popular photorealistic model for people and scenes that runs on small GPUs.
suggestions.howToUse: Author settings: Euler A or DPM++ 2M Karras, CFG 3.5 to 7, and the sd-vae-ft-mse VAE (see Quality below) to avoid artifacts. For a sharper result, use hires fix with the 4x-UltraSharp upscaler at denoise 0.25 to 0.7. The author supplies a long negative prompt that starts: (deformed iris, deformed pupils, semi-realistic, cgi, 3d, render, sketch, cartoon, drawing, anime:1.4), text, cropped, worst quality, low quality.
suggestions.license: CreativeML OpenRAIL-M

suggestions.name: AbsoluteReality 1.8.1
suggestions.what: A photorealistic SD 1.5 model with natural faces and good detail.
suggestions.howToUse: Author settings: CFG 4.5 to 10, 25 to 30 steps with DPM++ SDE Karras, and CLIP skip 2. Keep prompts simple, because long prompts can look less realistic. Do not use face restore. Add hires fix (denoise about 0.45, 20 steps) for more detail.
suggestions.license: Civitai terms: generated images may be sold; merges and derivatives allowed

suggestions.name: RealVisXL V5.0
suggestions.what: A photorealistic SDXL model for portraits and scenes.
suggestions.howToUse: Author settings: DPM++ SDE Karras with 30 or more steps, or DPM++ 2M Karras with 50 or more steps. Recommended negative prompt: bad hands, bad anatomy, ugly, deformed, (face asymmetry, eyes asymmetry, deformed eyes, deformed mouth, open mouth). For hires fix: 25 or more steps, denoise 0.1 to 0.3, upscale 1.1 to 1.5.
suggestions.license: CreativeML OpenRAIL++-M

suggestions.name: Juggernaut XL (Ragnarok)
suggestions.what: A well-known SDXL model for photorealism that also handles digital painting.
suggestions.howToUse: Author settings: 832x1216 for portraits (any SDXL size works), DPM++ 2M SDE sampler, 30 to 40 steps, CFG 3 to 6 (lower is a bit more realistic). Start with no negative prompt and add only what you do not want to see. The VAE is already included.
suggestions.license: Civitai terms: generated images may be sold; merges and derivatives allowed; credit the author

suggestions.name: Counterfeit V3.0
suggestions.what: A high quality anime-style SD 1.5 model.
suggestions.howToUse: The author gives no settings on the model page. The trigger word listed there is "girl". The EasyNegative embedding (see Quality below) was trained with this model, so it is a good first negative prompt. Otherwise try DPM++ 2M Karras, 20 to 30 steps, CFG 7 as a generic start.
suggestions.license: CreativeML OpenRAIL-M

suggestions.name: DreamShaper 8
suggestions.what: A flexible art and illustration model that does anime, fantasy and some photo styles.
suggestions.howToUse: Author notes: CLIP skip 2 works, do not use "restore faces", and most examples used hires fix or a second img2img pass at higher resolution. No fixed sampler is given; DPM++ 2M Karras, 25 steps, CFG 7 is a generic start. For a more anime look you may need to raise the weight of anime words in your prompt.
suggestions.license: Civitai terms: generated images may be sold; merges and derivatives allowed

suggestions.name: Animagine XL 4.0 Opt
suggestions.what: An anime-themed SDXL model trained on tag-style prompts.
suggestions.howToUse: Write tags in this order: 1girl/1boy, character name, series, rating, everything else, then end with: masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres. Author settings: Euler Ancestral, 25 to 28 steps, CFG 4 to 7 (5 recommended), sizes such as 832x1216 or 1024x1024. Suggested negative: lowres, bad anatomy, bad hands, text, error, missing finger, extra digits, fewer digits, cropped, worst quality, low quality, low score, bad score, average score, signature, watermark, username, blurry.
suggestions.license: CreativeML OpenRAIL++-M

suggestions.name: Animagine XL 3.1
suggestions.what: An earlier, widely used anime-themed SDXL model with strong character knowledge.
suggestions.howToUse: Write tags as: 1girl/1boy, character name, series, everything else. Add at the start: masterpiece, best quality, very aesthetic, absurdres. Author settings: Euler Ancestral, fewer than 30 steps, CFG 5 to 7. Suggested negative: nsfw, lowres, (bad), text, error, fewer, extra, missing, worst quality, jpeg artifacts, low quality, watermark, signature.
suggestions.license: CreativeML OpenRAIL++-M

suggestions.name: Detail Tweaker LoRA
suggestions.what: A small LoRA that adds or removes fine detail (skin, hair, fabric) without changing the subject.
suggestions.howToUse: Works with most SD 1.5 models. Positive weights add detail and negative weights reduce it, anywhere from -2 to 2; start around 0.5 to 1. The author does not give a trigger word. Its page notes that a negative weight also softens the harsh contrast some realistic models have.

suggestions.name: Add More Details
suggestions.what: A tiny LoRA that adds fine detail to faces, skin and textures.
suggestions.howToUse: The author recommends a weight between 0.5 and 1, or lower than 0.5 for a subtle effect. Negative weights sometimes give interesting results. It has no trigger word.

suggestions.name: Detail Tweaker XL
suggestions.what: A LoRA for SDXL that adds or removes fine detail such as skin texture.
suggestions.howToUse: Works with weights from -3 to 3. Positive adds detail, negative reduces it. The author recommends starting at 1.5 and adjusting based on your prompt and step count. No trigger word.

suggestions.name: DetailedEyes XL
suggestions.what: A LoRA that makes eyes, faces and skin more detailed on SDXL models, including anime ones.
suggestions.howToUse: The author says it should fit any SDXL model and adds detailed eyes, face and skin. It has less effect when the prompt is longer than 75 tokens. No trigger word or weight is given, so start at 0.7 to 1 and adjust.

suggestions.name: EasyNegative
suggestions.what: A negative embedding that lowers common flaws like bad hands and muddy detail in one word.
suggestions.howToUse: Put "easynegative" in the NEGATIVE prompt. Adjust its strength to taste, it scales well. It was trained with Counterfeit, so it suits anime and illustration models best. For photorealism, the AbsoluteReality author advises not using it.
suggestions.license: Civitai terms: generated images may be sold; merges and derivatives allowed

suggestions.name: sd-vae-ft-mse (SD 1.5 VAE)
suggestions.what: The standard improved VAE for SD 1.5; fixes washed-out colours and small artifacts on models without a built-in VAE.
suggestions.howToUse: Select it as the VAE if your SD 1.5 checkpoint has none built in. The Realistic Vision 5.1 author specifically recommends it. Checkpoints whose names say "VAE" or "baked" already include one.
suggestions.license: MIT

suggestions.name: SDXL VAE (fp16 fix)
suggestions.what: The SDXL VAE modified so it can decode in half precision without producing black or broken images.
suggestions.howToUse: Select it as the VAE for SDXL checkpoints that have no VAE built in, or if you see black or noisy images at fp16. Most popular SDXL checkpoints already include a VAE, so it is optional.
suggestions.license: MIT

suggestions.name: negativeXL
suggestions.what: A negative embedding for SDXL that reduces common flaws.
suggestions.howToUse: Put "negativeXL_D" in the NEGATIVE prompt (version D). The page gives no strength or other settings, so use it at default weight and lower it if images look flat.
